speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool? Have you had any recent travel or contact with anyone who has had similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent use of levofloxacin for pneumonia, is there a possibility that this diarrhea is a side effect or related to an infection like *C. difficile*? Have you had any fever or felt generally weak during this episode? REQUEST TEST: Stool for C. difficile toxin.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Stool for C. difficile toxin: Pending

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern; given your recent levofloxacin use and the severity of your symptoms, *Clostridioides difficile* infection is the leading suspicion. While we await the stool test results, I need to know if you are currently experiencing a fever or if your abdominal pain has become severe enough to prevent you from walking.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) secondary to recent levofloxacin therapy. I am requesting the immediate results of the Stool for C. difficile toxin test and any available abdominal imaging to confirm the diagnosis and assess for complications.
